reachable_path: An actual private local runtime can enqueue a local message: worker_runtime.py.diff D02:608–643 supports enqueue_outbox and binds its task/request, then D02:666–668 commits category outbox into local storage.
A pending legacy message for another, unbound task can coexist in the same repository's _outbox/event_outbox; the ordinary enqueue writer is task-targeted and the stores are separate.
Outside a private local scope, claim_outbox_message() has no task argument. _local_target nevertheless returns True if ANY local outbox row exists, irrespective of its task or status.
dispatch raises ValueError at protocol.py:224 before original legacy selection. The storage-level guard repeats the same test. Thus neither backend can claim the unrelated eligible legacy message.
Because the predicate tests existence, a retained local row continues to block legacy claims after its local status changes.
finding.impact: One operational task can starve unrelated legacy message delivery in a shared event repository. This is availability/compatibility failure, not an authority bypass.
finding.requested_resolution: Have Astra define a candidate-specific, lock/transaction-protected legacy claim path that cannot claim an operational task, while preserving private local claiming. Do not merely remove the operational fence.
expected_regression_cases: Both Memory and SQLite: retain a local outbox row and enqueue an unrelated eligible legacy message; the public claim must obtain only the legacy message and leave local data/receipts unchanged.
Repeat with the local row no longer PENDING to ensure historical local rows do not globally disable legacy claims.
Retain negative coverage proving public claims/mutations never acquire or modify a local operational message and private local claims still require a current scope.
Exercise the candidate check under the actual storage lock/transaction so a binding change cannot turn the fix into a check/use race.
